enhanced_information: Complement functions include lysis, chemotaxis, and opsonization, all of which are part of the immune response. Lysis involves the destruction of pathogens, chemotaxis refers to the movement of immune cells towards the site of infection, and opsonization enhances phagocytosis by marking pathogens. Glycolysis, however, is a metabolic process involving the breakdown of glucose for energy production and is not related to complement function. Therefore, glycolysis is the correct answer as it is not a function of the complement system.
analysis: The complement system is a part of the immune system that enhances the ability to clear microbes and damaged cells. Its functions include lysis, chemotaxis, and opsonization. Lysis refers to the destruction of pathogens, chemotaxis involves the attraction of immune cells to the site of infection, and opsonization marks pathogens for phagocytosis. Glycolysis, on the other hand, is a metabolic process that breaks down glucose to produce energy and is not related to the immune functions of the complement system. Therefore, glycolysis is not a function of the complement system.
